title: There’s No Such Thing as Self-Sabotage
coreMove: A damaging pattern usually protects a hidden need; name the payoff, respect what it tried to guard, then take one action that meets the need without keeping the damage.

exampleSpecs.audience: a promoted manager who starts creating drama after success
exampleSpecs.stakes: a good week can become a crisis if the old ceiling retakes control
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Expose the payoff behind upper-limit doubt.

exampleSpecs.audience: a person whose stated goal and hidden loyalty conflict
exampleSpecs.stakes: stated desire cannot win while the protected objective stays unnamed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Reveal the subconscious objective beneath the stated goal.

exampleSpecs.audience: a reader whose spending creates brief relief
exampleSpecs.stakes: budgeting alone misses the need the purchases are soothing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Translate spending into the need it serves.

exampleSpecs.audience: an overworker learning what stillness exposes
exampleSpecs.stakes: productivity can hide an emotional problem until rest becomes unbearable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show overwork as avoidance, not passion.

exampleSpecs.audience: a person replaying an old attachment pattern
exampleSpecs.stakes: a quick contact hit can keep an old wound in charge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Connect the contact loop to attachment need.

exampleSpecs.audience: a person who confuses relief with alignment
exampleSpecs.stakes: relief can protect invisibility while shrinking the future
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Move from hidden commitment to tolerable action.
